I am a 49-year-old woman farmer in Dongfu village, Anzhai township, Quzhou County. I have been farming since I was a teenager, and my family has about 4 mu of good flat land. I never went to school, so I cannot read the labels on fertilizer bags very well, but I know farming from my hands and from watching my neighbors.

The wheat is already in the ground — we sowed it last October after the National Day holiday, as everyone does here. I used the improved wheat seed called "shimai" that I bought from the seed shop in town. I rotavated the soil before sowing. For the wheat, I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time, and I will topdress with urea when the wheat turns yellow at jointing stage. I irrigate four times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading. The water comes from our tube well, and pumping costs money, so I watch the sky, but four times is what we always do. I also spray pesticides three or four times — herbicide once early on, and insecticide two or three times when I see aphids or other bugs. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu if the weather cooperates, which is what my neighbors usually get.

Right after we harvest the wheat in early June, we have only a few days to get the maize in the ground before the summer heat peaks. We never till for maize — there is no time, and everyone here plants maize no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid maize seed, usually "nongda372" or something similar from the shop. For maize, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, about 50 jin, and that is usually enough. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet leaf stage. Maize needs spraying about four times — herbicide once, insecticide two or three times for corn borers. I expect around 1,100 to 1,200 jin per mu.

I thought about growing cotton on one mu because the price looked good last year, but cotton needs too much pesticide — my neighbor sprays more than ten times — and my husband and I are getting older. We cannot manage all that labor. So all four mu will stay in the wheat-maize rotation. It is safe, and we always have grain to eat and some to sell.
